exhibits.title: The Patchwork Loom
exhibits.text: A great loom stands where two wings meet. On its frame hangs a square of enchanted cloth — the noisy latent, a grid 32 tall, 32 wide, and 4 layers deep — and the loom's task is to feed it to a transformer that eats only THREADS, only a sequence of tokens, and knows nothing of grids. So the loom cuts. It runs blades across the cloth in a fixed mesh of patch size 2x2, dividing the 32x32 face into (32/2)x(32/2) = 16x16 = 256 little squares. Each square is small — 2 rows by 2 columns by 4 channels — and holds exactly 2*2*4 = 16 numbers. The loom FLATTENS each square into a strand of 16 values, then passes it through a single learned linear projection that lengthens it to d_model. Out the far side come 256 threads, each of dimension d_model: a sequence at last. This rite has a true name, and it is not new to this castle — it is PATCHIFY, the very same tokenization the Attention wing performed on images with ViT and SmolVLM. A picture, a latent, a page of pixels: all become tokens the same way, by being cut into patches and projected. The loom is the mirror-image of the machine at the wing's end that will sew the threads back into cloth; here we only cut. And a cut sequence has lost something the grid never had to state aloud — WHERE each square once hung. That debt is paid at the next station, where positions are woven back in.

exhibits.title: The Cut — Grid to Sequence
exhibits.text: Follow one strand end to end. INPUT: a latent of shape (32, 32, 4). CHOOSE a patch size p = 2. The face tiles into (32/p) x (32/p) = 16 x 16 = 256 non-overlapping patches. EACH patch has shape (2, 2, 4), which is 2*2*4 = 16 scalar values. FLATTEN those 16 values into a vector. PROJECT with one shared learned matrix W of shape (16, d_model), so every patch-vector of length 16 becomes a token of length d_model. RESULT: a tensor (256, d_model) — 256 tokens, ready for plain transformer blocks. This is precisely ViT patchification carried over from the Attention wing, unchanged: patchify does not care whether the grid holds RGB pixels or diffusion latents. It is the bridge that lets the transformer machinery of one wing operate inside the diffusion framework of another, with the network's guts borrowed whole and nothing bolted on.

exhibits.title: The Lost Address — Why Positions Are Essential
exhibits.text: The moment the loom cuts, a subtle theft occurs: the sequence is an unordered SET. A transformer is permutation-equivariant — it measures only the CONTENT similarity of tokens, so shuffle the 256 threads and the raw attention gives the same answer. To a transformer, the patch that hung at the top-left corner (0,0) and the patch at the far corner (15,15) are indistinguishable once flattened — same-length vectors, no address attached. A convolution never had this problem: it slides a kernel across the grid and so inherently KNOWS spatial layout. A transformer does not. So after patchify we ADD a positional embedding to each token, one per patch coordinate, teaching (0,0) that it is (0,0). This is exactly the permutation-invariance met in the Attention wing and answered in the basement chamber 'The Wheel of Frequencies' — the sinusoidal clock and RoPE. DiT rests on those same sinusoids: give each token its place, or the denoiser cannot tell a corner of the image from its center.

exhibits.title: The Mirror Seam — Unpatchify
exhibits.text: Every cut anticipates a stitch. At the far end of the DiT wing, after the transformer has done its thinking, a final linear layer projects each of the 256 tokens back down to 2*2*4 = 16 values, and UNPATCHIFY reassembles them into the grid they came from: 256 patches sewn back into a (32, 32, 4) latent — the predicted noise, in the very shape of the input. Patchify compresses grid to sequence; unpatchify expands sequence back to grid. The two are mirror images, like the descending and ascending arms of a U-Net — except here there is NO convolution, no down-sampling, no skip connections. Just cut, think, sew. Shape in equals shape out: (32, 32, 4) enters the wing and (32, 32, 4) leaves it, an interchangeable denoiser slotted into the same diffusion framework the U-Net once filled.

exhibits.title: Patchify: Grid to Tokens, Then Positions
exhibits.spec:
graph TD
  A[latent grid 32x32x4] --> B[cut into 2x2 patches]
  B --> C[16x16 = 256 patches]
  C --> D[each patch: 2x2x4 = 16 values]
  D --> E[flatten + linear project to d_model]
  E --> F[256 tokens of dim d_model]
  F --> G[ADD positional embedding per patch]
  G --> H[ordered sequence for transformer blocks]
  H -. mirror at wing's end .-> I[unpatchify: 256 tokens back to 32x32x4]
exhibits.caption: A latent grid is cut into 256 patches, each flattened and projected to a d_model token; positional embeddings restore the address the set has lost. Unpatchify is the same path run backward — no conv, no down-sampling, just the mirror seam.

exhibits.title: The Loom's Cut, Traced Thread by Thread
exhibits.caption: Watch the loom work. The 32x32x4 latent is scored on a fixed 2x2 mesh into 16x16 = 256 little squares (a). Follow one square through the shuttle (b): its 2*2*4 = 16 numbers are flattened into a strand, then a single shared learned matrix W lengthens that strand to d_model — one patch becomes one token. Out the far side runs an ordered thread of 256 tokens (c), read in row-major order: (0,0), (0,1), (0,2), and on. Panel (d) is the weaver's choice of blade: patch size p trades detail against length — p=2 yields 256 tokens (fine, costly), p=4 yields 64, p=8 only 16 (coarse, cheap). DiT-XL/2 keeps the finest blade, p=2. This is ViT patchification unchanged, carried whole from the Attention wing.
